abstract:
INTRODUCTIONThe precuneus, a metamemory-related parietal region with sex-specific vulnerability in Alzheimers disease (AD), may contribute to reduced insight of memory deficit. We investigated whether precuneus structural integrity explained sex differences in subjective-objective memory discrepancy.

METHODSPrecuneus volumes, as well as three other control regions, were acquired in 350 A{beta}+ and 310 A{beta}-participants from the ADNI dataset to quantify within-individual changes in subjective-objective memory discrepancy across AD progression.

RESULTSA{beta}+ participants exhibited steeper objective memory decline ({beta} = -0.446, p < 0.001) despite stable subjective complaints ({beta} = -0.027, p = 0.587), resulting in a widening subjective-objective memory discrepancy ({beta} = 0.317, p < 0.001). In this group, only precuneus atrophy showed a sex-dependent association with discrepancy ({beta} = 0.508, p = 0.002), a finding absent in the A{beta}- group or other brain regions.

DISCUSSIONThe precuneus represents a neuroanatomical substrate associated with sex-related differences in metacognitive vulnerability in A{beta}+ individuals.
